strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem formulation with an intuitive solution combining local feature matching and monocular depth priors
Mathematically sound scale-aware Procrustes alignment framework with correct derivation of scale recovery from correspondences
Strong empirical results showing 26% improvement in cross-area localization error on KITTI compared to prior art
Practical design that works with different depth predictors without per-model finetuning and maintains reasonable computational efficiency
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including ablation studies, multiple scenarios (known/unknown orientation, same/cross-area), and both metric and relative depth
Transparent discussion of limitations and honest presentation of failure cases with visual examples
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components (local feature matching, monocular depth, Procrustes alignment) are well-established; the contribution is primarily their combination without substantial innovation

Restrictive similarity transform assumption (uniform scale, rotation, translation) is not thoroughly validated; breaks down with perspective distortion and partial occlusions but limited analysis of when/why it holds
Critical dependency on external monocular depth predictor quality; limited analysis of how depth errors propagate through the pipeline or systematic study of failure modes from poor depth
Narrow and dated baseline comparisons (most from 2021-2022) with missing comparisons to recent transformer-based and sophisticated deep learning approaches

Insufficient analysis of feature matching reliability: ground and aerial views are drastically different (perspective vs. orthographic), yet limited evaluation of feature matching failures or robustness to repetitive textures
Limited generalization study with evaluation confined to two datasets (KITTI, VIGOR) and urban driving scenarios; no evaluation across geographic regions, seasonal variations, or temporal changes
Incomplete scale recovery validation: Table 4 shows consistency but doesn't validate absolute scale against ground truth; claims about enabling different depth models lack thorough validation
Reproducibility concerns: code not released, depth thresholds lack justification (described as visual inspection), parameter selection process incompletely specified
Arbitrary experimental choices with insufficient justification (matching score thresholds, depth thresholds, dustbin row/column dropping)
Missing ablation on whether learning-based pose regression underperforms feature matching, and no analysis decomposing failures into depth vs. feature matching components

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing a clear limitation of prior work (information loss in BEV transformation) with a principled solution using depth priors for correspondence matching
Sound and rigorous technical approach with correct mathematical formulation of scale-aware Procrustes alignment, enabling consistent scale recovery from relative depth
Comprehensive experimental validation on two diverse datasets (KITTI, VIGOR) with strong baselines, achieving state-of-the-art results including 26% error reduction on cross-area generalization
Excellent practical flexibility: plug-and-play compatibility with different depth models without fine-tuning, works with both metric and relative depth
Thorough ablation studies validating design choices (Table 3), extensive appendix with failure case analysis, runtime/memory benchmarking, and reproducibility details
Superior generalization to challenging scenarios including cross-area and unknown orientation settings, demonstrating robustness beyond in-distribution performance
Exceptional presentation quality with effective visualizations, clear problem formulation, logical organization, and informative qualitative results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines well-established components (feature matching, Procrustes alignment, depth prediction) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts
Fundamental dependency on monocular depth predictor quality with no proposed solutions for handling unreliable depth regions; performance ceiling is bounded by depth estimation accuracy
Insufficient analysis of failure modes: main paper lacks detailed discussion of when/why the method fails; appendix shows failures but provides minimal explanation or systematic categorization
Restrictive scene assumptions (exact similarity transform) not thoroughly validated; impact of violations due to complex geometry, occlusions, and perspective distortions is underexplored
Limited comparisons with recent deep learning approaches; most baselines are from 2021-2023, missing more recent transformer-based methods for cross-view localization
Method shows sensitivity to depth filtering parameters (Table 4) despite claims of robustness; limited guidance for parameter selection in new domains
Scalability concerns: experiments on bounded urban areas; unclear performance on larger regions, diverse environments, or non-urban scenes
Shallow analysis of orientation estimation: limited investigation of systematic biases or conditions causing orientation failures versus localization failures

strengths: Interpretable method: Analytically derived pose from local feature correspondences allows direct visualization of alignment quality, providing intuitive understanding of localization performance
Comprehensive experimental validation: Evaluations on KITTI, VIGOR, and CVACT with extensive ablation studies examining hyperparameters, depth predictors, and design choices
Technically sound: Clear mathematical formulation (scale-aware Procrustes alignment) with proofs, detailed implementation details, and reproducibility considerations
Practical applicability: No pixel-level annotations required during training; achieves competitive runtime (0.42 FPS with RANSAC filtering)
Well-presented results: Clear visualization of successful alignments and failure cases; attempts cross-dataset generalization
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Combines existing well-established components (local feature matching, monocular depth lifting, Procrustes alignment) with straightforward mathematical formulation. The scale-aware variant lacks innovative insight

Modest empirical improvements: KITTI results show performance below or comparable to baselines (SliceMatch, HC-Net). VIGOR improvements are incremental (0.5-2m in many metrics). No statistical significance testing provided

Questionable weak supervision claim: Method depends on pre-trained depth models at inference; these models themselves trained on pixel-level annotations. Not truly end-to-end; performance bottleneck between depth vs. features unclear

Unvalidated fundamental assumptions: Scale factor derivation assumes metric depth is reliable, but monocular predictors are poorly calibrated to metric scale. Why metric depth works better than relative depth not adequately explained. Impact of depth prediction errors on pose not analyzed

Limited evaluation scope: Only urban environments tested; no evaluation on rural, night-time, or adverse weather. CVACT dataset lacks quantitative results. Failure case analysis is minimal and lacks actionable insights

Experimental concerns: Incomplete baseline comparisons in Table 2; different RANSAC thresholds for different datasets; no ablation on feature extractor choice; hyperparameter selections (depth threshold, temperature) appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis

Weakened interpretability claims: Full pipeline relies on learned DINOv2 features and pre-trained depth models (black boxes); analytically derived pose is only partially interpretable. Dependency on frozen external models contradicts claim of full interpretability

Missing practical analysis: No breakdown of computational costs (feature extraction, depth prediction, matching, pose estimation); memory usage not justified; deployment feasibility on edge devices not discussed; variance across RANSAC random seeds not reported

strengths: Novel integration of local feature matching with depth-lifted BEV alignment provides an elegant solution to cross-view localization that avoids pixel-level annotations while maintaining interpretability
Rigorous mathematical framework with scale-aware Procrustes alignment (thorough SVD-based derivation in Appendix G) that naturally handles unknown scale through principled weighting
Strong empirical results with substantial improvements over baselines (KITTI: 3.64m vs 9.10m for FG² under ±10° noise; VIGOR competitive performance) and consistent gains across multiple datasets
Exceptional interpretability advantage demonstrated through visual correspondence overlays and strong empirical correlation between correspondence quality and localization accuracy

Comprehensive experimental validation including extensive ablation studies systematically analyzing design choices, multiple datasets (KITTI, VIGOR, CVACT), challenging scenarios (±180° orientation, cross-area tests), and cross-dataset generalization
Practical flexibility: method works with different depth predictors (metric/relative depth) without retraining, with only ~0.2m degradation when using relative depth at inference
Novel RANSAC-based outlier detection via correspondence quality that improves over traditional approaches (~25% relative error reduction in Table 7)
Strong reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, explicit loss formulations, and commitment to code release
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components (DINOv2, monocular depth estimation, Procrustes alignment are standard); main contribution is their integration with scale-aware weighting—somewhat incremental

Absolute localization errors remain substantial for precision applications (3.64m mean, 1.64m median on KITTI same-area; 9.30m mean, 1.93m median under ±180° orientation), limiting real-world deployment for high-accuracy scenarios

Critical dependency on depth estimation quality with insufficient analysis of error propagation; scale estimation (Eq. 5) sensitivity to depth outliers not characterized; no analysis of failure modes when depth predictions fail
Still requires ground-truth pose and depth during training despite 'weak supervision' claims; testing on relative depth without retraining (Appendix F) shows performance gaps—not truly unsupervised

Poor cross-area generalization: VIGOR cross-area results lack quantitative error metrics, CVACT generalization shown only qualitatively without actual localization error numbers; limits real-world applicability where training/test areas differ

Insufficient analysis of failure modes: dense vegetation limitations (Fig. 10) identified but not deeply analyzed; no clear guidance on success/failure conditions; failure rate on realistic scenarios not characterized
Computational performance concerns: 0.42 FPS with RANSAC is slow for real-time applications; 14.74 FPS without RANSAC still includes depth overhead; no runtime comparison with FG²
Lack of theoretical justification for why scale-aware Procrustes outperforms standard approach; correlation between correspondence quality and pose accuracy is empirical without theoretical bounds
Baseline comparison limitations: most comparisons with very recent methods (2023-24); missing well-established classical baselines; FG² comparison lacks depth; no comparison with SfM-based methods
Presentation: paper is lengthy (27 pages) with critical details relegated to appendix (relative depth training, additional ablations); dense notation in methodology sections
